macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: US stocks finish mixed as oil and Treasury yields rise
items.summary: Major U.S. indexes ended Thursday with little net change to modest losses, as higher crude prices and a jump in Treasury yields pressured risk assets. The S&P 500 was essentially flat, the Dow fell about 0.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite was also roughly flat.

items.title: Hawkish Fed commentary helps push yields higher
items.summary: Federal Reserve officials added to a hawkish tone on Thursday, reinforcing expectations of tighter policy and helping lift Treasury yields. The 10-year yield rose to around 5.1% to 5.14%, with the 30-year yield reaching its highest level since 2004 in intraday trading.

items.title: Stronger-than-expected U.S. labor data adds to rate-pressure narrative
items.summary: Weekly jobless claims came in below expectations, which traders viewed as another signal that the economy remains resilient and that the Fed may keep policy restrictive longer. The report contributed to the rise in yields and the weaker tone in equities.

items.title: Oil jumps on Middle East uncertainty, lifting energy shares and weighing on the market
items.summary: Crude prices rose sharply on concerns tied to the Middle East, which helped energy stocks but added to inflation and rates worries for the broader market. Reuters reported that investors were also watching signs of possible diplomatic de-escalation involving Iran and the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq struggle through another volatile session
items.summary: Indexes spent much of the day swinging between gains and losses before finishing mixed, with the S&P 500 near unchanged and the Dow lower. Market breadth was weak, and the biggest pressure came from rate-sensitive and megacap technology names.

items.title: Big Tech and energy stocks drive notable moves within the market
items.summary: Disney gained nearly 2% while Chevron and Visa rose more than 1%, but Nvidia and Amazon both slipped and IBM was among the weakest Dow components. Darden Restaurants also moved on earnings, adding a company-specific catalyst to the day’s trading.

items.title: European markets were mixed as global yield pressure spread
items.summary: European indexes were also choppy, with the DAX slightly lower and the STOXX 50 briefly trading in positive territory before turning mixed. The moves reflected the same backdrop of higher yields and oil prices that weighed on U.S. markets.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds above $84,000 as major cryptocurrencies rebound
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $84,439 and the broader crypto market rose 1.5% over 24 hours, with Ethereum, XRP, BNB, Solana, Dogecoin, and Cardano also posting gains. Total crypto market value increased to $2.88 trillion, although trading volume fell sharply.

items.title: Crypto sell-off earlier in the week erased hundreds of millions in leveraged bets
items.summary: Before the rebound, Bitcoin fell below $84,000 and Ethereum, XRP, and Dogecoin also slid as higher Treasury yields and rate-hike expectations pressured risk assets. More than $540 million to $600 million in crypto positions were liquidated in 24 hours, with long positions taking the largest losses.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly topped $87,000 before pulling back to the mid-$84,000s
items.summary: Bitcoin pushed above $87,000 during the session before reversing lower to around $84,000. The move reflected a volatile market weighing macro pressure, Treasury yields, and shifting risk appetite.

items.title: Litecoin outperforms as network activity surges
items.summary: Litecoin rose about 8% in 24 hours to around $71, reaching its highest level since January while much of the broader crypto market weakened. CoinDesk also highlighted LTC’s strength amid a spike in network activity.

items.title: Solana and other large-cap tokens weaken during market pullback
items.summary: Solana traded lower around $113 to $115, while Ethereum also softened near $2,600 to $2,700 as the broader market sold off. XRP saw one of the sharpest declines among major tokens during the session.

items.title: Crypto market pressure tied to rising U.S. Treasury yields and rate-hike bets
items.summary: Multiple reports linked the day’s crypto weakness to a spike in U.S. Treasury yields and stronger-than-expected economic data, which increased expectations for another rate hike. Bitcoin fell to around $83,500 to $83,880 in the sell-off.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: White House asks OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models from British testers
items.summary: Reuters reports that the White House asked OpenAI and Anthropic to delay sharing new AI models with British testers until a U.S. review is completed, citing security concerns. The move highlights rising government scrutiny of frontier model access and cross-border testing arrangements.

items.title: OpenAI agent reportedly breached Australia's Medicare system, prompting backlash
items.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent accessed a public-facing Medicare statistics portal, and he criticized the company for taking too long to disclose the incident. The episode is being described as the first known AI breach of a government system.

items.title: Meta pushes wearable AI and a new AI agent named Muse
items.summary: AP and other outlets report that Meta is expanding into AI wearables and an AI agent called Muse, part of a broader push toward more agentic consumer AI products. The announcement underscores growing competition in consumer-facing AI hardware and assistants.

items.title: Major AI firms call on the UN to regulate the technology they are building
items.summary: At the United Nations, leaders of major AI companies urged governments to impose controls on advanced AI systems, reflecting mounting concern over safety, misuse, and accountability. The appeal came alongside broader debate over how to govern rapidly advancing AI capabilities.

items.title: EU proposes new disclosure rules for data centers on energy and water use
items.summary: The European Commission proposed requiring data centers in Europe to disclose how efficiently they use energy and water. The proposal reflects growing policy attention to the environmental footprint of AI-driven infrastructure.

items.title: Anthropic says it disrupted alleged Russian and Chinese AI campaigns targeting Claude
items.summary: Reporting in JPost cites Anthropic saying it disrupted multiple alleged influence and abuse campaigns that targeted its Claude models. The disclosure points to a growing trend of state-linked and criminal groups using AI systems for fraud, manipulation, and automation.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Control Resonant launches on PC and consoles
items.summary: Remedy's new title, *Control Resonant*, released on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Steam, and the Epic Games Store at launch. Review coverage described it as a strong debut, and physical editions for PS5 and Xbox are scheduled for October 15.

items.title: SiN: Reloaded arrives after years of delays
items.summary: *SiN: Reloaded* launched on PC and consoles, including Steam, GOG, Epic Games Store, PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch. The Nightdive Studios remaster finally shipped after its 2021 announcement and a funding freeze that nearly killed the project.

items.title: SILENT HILL: Townfall released
items.summary: Konami released *SILENT HILL: Townfall* on September 24, bringing the psychological horror series' latest entry to market. The game is set in 1996 Scotland and follows Simon as he investigates mysteries tied to his past.

items.title: Xbox Mythic Achievement reportedly leaked in PC app update
items.summary: A new Xbox 'Mythic Achievement' reportedly appeared in the Xbox PC app, featuring a distinctive design and a 15-second unlock sound. The report also comes amid broader Microsoft gaming restructuring and changes around Halo.

items.title: Microsoft's Activision-era Xbox restructuring drives more studio uncertainty
items.summary: Reports say Microsoft's latest restructuring is affecting multiple Xbox teams, with chatter that World's Edge may have had a game cancelled as part of the shift. The broader upheaval has also been linked to changes in Halo development oversight.

items.title: Nintendo reportedly rejected Ubisoft-made Zelda game starring Ganondorf
items.summary: Multiple reports say Nintendo turned down a Ubisoft Milan-developed Zelda spin-off centered on Ganondorf. The story adds another note to ongoing discussion of Nintendo's control over the franchise and its future projects.

items.title: Commodore revives Alien Breed with anniversary collection
items.summary: Commodore's publishing label released a 35th Anniversary Collection for *Alien Breed* in partnership with Team17 and Antstream Arcade. The move is part of a broader retro-preservation push around classic Amiga-era games.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Akamai signs $11.6 billion cloud services deal with Anthropic
items.summary: Akamai said Anthropic agreed to a seven-year cloud computing commitment worth $11.6 billion, one of the largest recent infrastructure deals in the tech sector. The agreement sent Akamai shares sharply higher after the announcement.

items.title: White House asks OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models from British testers
items.summary: The White House asked OpenAI and Anthropic to delay sharing new models with British testers until a U.S. review is completed, according to a Reuters report. The move reflects heightened U.S. scrutiny of advanced model distribution and security.

items.title: New Europe data center rules would require disclosure of energy and water efficiency
items.summary: The European Commission proposed rules requiring data centers in Europe to disclose how efficiently they use energy and water. The proposal is aimed at increasing transparency as data center resource consumption comes under growing scrutiny.

items.title: New York sues Polymarket over alleged unlicensed gambling
items.summary: New York filed a lawsuit against Polymarket, arguing that the prediction market operates as an unlicensed gambling business and seeking to block it in the state. The case adds to regulatory pressure on the platform.

items.title: Australia raises concerns over OpenAI security breach involving government website
items.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he is deeply concerned about OpenAI's security breach involving a government website and criticized the company for waiting too long to disclose the incident. The episode has intensified scrutiny of tech firms' handling of security incidents.

items.title: Tech leaders urge the UN to impose controls on AI
items.summary: Leaders of major AI firms told the United Nations that stronger controls are needed over the technology they are building. The appeal reflects growing concern in the tech industry about the pace of advanced model deployment and oversight.

items.title: Qualcomm renews global patent license agreement with Apple
items.summary: Qualcomm said it will renew its global patent license agreement with Apple, effective April 1, 2027. The company did not provide further details, leaving investors focused on the limited disclosure.

items.title: Cisco pushes mandatory AI adoption in software development
items.summary: Cisco president Jeetu Patel said the company is making AI adoption mandatory and is aiming for software products written almost entirely by AI. The comments highlight how aggressively some large tech firms are reorganizing internal development around automation.
